questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A body is in equilibrium under the action of three concurrent forces. This is possible only if:
options: All three forces are equal in magnitude
They all act in the same direction
questions.explanation: For translational equilibrium the resultant must vanish, so the three force vectors drawn head to tail form a closed triangle.
questions.ncertReference: Physics Class 11, Chapter 4: Laws of Motion

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: According to Wien's displacement law, as the temperature of a black body rises, the wavelength of maximum emission:
options: Decreases, shifting towards the blue end
questions.explanation: λm T is a constant, so a hotter body glows from red through yellow to bluish white, which is how the surface temperature of stars is estimated.
questions.ncertReference: Physics Class 11, Chapter 10: Thermal Properties of Matter

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: According to Malus' law, when completely plane polarised light of intensity I₀ passes through an analyser whose axis makes an angle θ with the plane of polarisation, the transmitted intensity is:
questions.explanation: Only the component of the amplitude along the analyser axis passes, and intensity goes as the square of amplitude, so I = I₀ cos² θ and the light vanishes at θ = 90°.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Two samples of pure water collected from different sources are found to contain hydrogen and oxygen in the same fixed mass ratio of 1 : 8. This illustrates the law of:
questions.explanation: The law of definite proportions says a given compound always has the same elements in the same proportion by mass, whatever its source or method of preparation.
questions.ncertReference: Chemistry Class 11, Chapter 1: Some Basic Concepts of Chemistry

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The Nernst equation for an electrode allows one to calculate the electrode potential at:
options: Equilibrium only, where the cell potential is maximum
questions.explanation: E = E° - (0.059/n) log[ ] at 298 K extends the standard potential to non-standard concentrations. At equilibrium the cell potential is zero, not maximum.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Aniline is a weaker base than ammonia because in aniline:
options: The lone pair on nitrogen is delocalised into the benzene ring
The ring releases electrons to nitrogen
questions.explanation: Resonance makes the lone pair less available for donation to a proton, so aniline is a far weaker base than aliphatic amines or ammonia.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question: Malonate inhibits the enzyme succinate dehydrogenase by resembling its substrate succinate. This is an example of:
questions.explanation: The inhibitor competes for the active site itself, so raising the substrate concentration can overcome it. This principle is used in many drugs.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question: In the cloning vector pBR322, the ori sequence is important because it:
options: Is the site where replication starts and controls copy number
Is cut by every restriction enzyme
Allows the vector to enter the nucleus
questions.explanation: Any linked DNA replicates along with the vector from this origin, and a vector with a high copy number ori gives many copies of the target gene.
questions.ncertReference: Biology Class 12, Chapter 9: Biotechnology: Principles and Processes

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: Bony fishes and aquatic amphibians excrete ammonia directly because:
options: Ammonia is the least toxic excretory product
Ammonia is highly soluble and plenty of water is available to dilute it
Ammonia needs the most energy to make
questions.explanation: Ammonia is the most toxic but needs no energy to convert, so it suits animals surrounded by water. Land animals make urea or uric acid to save water.
questions.ncertReference: Biology Class 11, Chapter 16: Excretory Products and their Elimination

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: In Drosophila, sex is determined by the XX-XY system. A human male produces two kinds of gametes with respect to sex chromosomes, so human sex determination is said to be:
questions.explanation: The human male makes X bearing and Y bearing sperms, so the father's gamete decides the sex of the child. In birds the female is heterogametic, ZW.
questions.ncertReference: Biology Class 12, Chapter 4: Principles of Inheritance and Variation
